title: Is Betelgeuse Really About to Explode?
description:
Is Betelgeuse About to Explode?
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vP1BbqZ_dnM

The orange star on Orion's shoulder is a dying red supergiant. One day Betelgeuse will blow itself apart as a supernova and shine so brightly for weeks that it will be visible in the daytime sky — but what do the 2019 Great Dimming and seismic models say about when?

Sources: Joyce et al. (2020), The Astrophysical Journal 902, 63 — Betelgeuse radius, mass, distance and core helium-burning stage (https://doi.org/10.3847/1538-4357/abb8db) · Montargès et al. (2021), Nature 594, 365–368 — the 2019–2020 Great Dimming dust veil (https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03546-8) · Goldberg, Bauer & Howell (2020), Research Notes of the AAS 4, 35 — Type IIP supernova plateau brightness at half-Moon scale (https://doi.org/10.3847/2515-5172/ab7c68).

Pictures: ESO/B. Tafreshi (twanight.org), R. Wesson/ESO, ESO/S. Brunier, and ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO) Orion and observatory time-lapses (CC BY 4.0), and ESO/M. Montargès et al. VLT/SPHERE image of Betelgeuse (CC BY 4.0), alongside original animated explainers and AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: ESO/B. Tafreshi (twanight.org, CC BY 4.0); R. Wesson/ESO (CC BY 4.0); ESO/S. Brunier (CC BY 4.0); ALMA (ESO/NAOJ/NRAO, CC BY 4.0); ESO/M. Montargès et al. (CC BY 4.0, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
